documents.title: Acute Visit - Fever and Sore Throat
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
20 y/o home from college for winter break. Two weeks of fevers, sore throat and exhaustion, same feel as his illnesses last January and July. OTC pain relievers and lozenges haven't touched it. Says his upper abdomen feels "puffy." No bleeding, bruising, dark urine or yellow eyes that he has noticed. Not taking any medications.

NKDA.

Exam: Febrile at 38.5, other vitals as charted. Pharynx red with exudate. Tender cervical nodes. Abdomen soft, spleen tip palpable, mildly enlarged, nontender. No jaundice. No petechiae or bruising on skin survey.

CBC this morning: Hgb 10.2, WBC 15.0, platelets 90K, 20% atypical lymphocytes. His August counts were normal.

A/P:
1. Third mononucleosis-like illness in a year, heterophile positive at the first two. Treating as a relapsing course of the same illness.
2. New anemia and thrombocytopenia. With mono the worry is immune destruction. Sent a smear for pathologist review, direct antiglobulin test, retic count, LDH, haptoglobin and bilirubin from this morning's draw; will call him with results this afternoon. Low threshold for same-day hematology input.
3. Spleen: no sports or lifting. Rest and fluids. Avoid ibuprofen and aspirin while platelets are low.
4. ED for bleeding, black stools, sudden left-sided belly pain, lightheadedness or shortness of breath.

orders.reason: Coombs-positive hemolytic anemia and thrombocytopenia with mononucleosis

documents.title: Results Call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Afternoon labs back. Smear reviewed by pathology, atypical lymphocytes confirmed. DAT positive. Retic 4.6%, LDH 388, haptoglobin <10, total bilirubin 1.9 with direct 0.3. Picture fits autoimmune hemolysis, along with the low platelets, in the setting of his mono.

Called patient. He feels the same as this morning, no bleeding, no dark urine, no chest pain or breathlessness. Explained the findings. Spoke with on-call hematology at the regional hospital: Hgb 10.2 and stable symptoms do not need admission or steroids tonight; they will see him early next week. Urgent referral placed.

Same precautions as this morning. ED for any bleeding, yellowing, cola-colored urine, faintness or worsening breathlessness. He verbalized understanding.

documents.title: Referral to Hematology
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Re: Min-jun Tanaka, DOB 12/12/2005

Thank you for seeing this 20-year-old college student, otherwise healthy, on no medications, NKDA. Heterophile-positive mononucleosis in January 2025 and again at an ED visit in July 2025, both resolving with supportive care. Normal CBC August 2025.

Seen today with 2 weeks of fever, sore throat and fatigue. T 38.5, exudative pharyngitis, tender cervical nodes, mild splenomegaly. Hgb 10.2, WBC 15.0, platelets 90K, atypical lymphocytes 20%, confirmed on smear. DAT positive. Retic 4.6%, LDH 388, haptoglobin <10, total bilirubin 1.9 (direct 0.3).

Discussed with your on-call physician today. Requesting evaluation of Coombs-positive hemolytic anemia and thrombocytopenia during a mononucleosis illness. Family history: maternal uncle with nasopharyngeal carcinoma, paternal grandfather with gastric cancer.

Copies of today's labs attached.

documents.title: Referral Scheduled
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hematology office called, referral received, pt scheduled Thursday 1/8 at 1:15. Called pt to confirm, he has it. Reminded him to bring his insurance card since it's a specialist.

documents.title: Hematology Consultation
documents.author: hematology
documents.body:
Outside hematology group. Date of consultation 01/08/2026. Received 01/09/2026.

Reason for referral: positive DAT with anemia and low platelets during infectious mononucleosis.

History: 20M, previously healthy, presented to his PCP 1/2 with two weeks of fever, pharyngitis and fatigue, his third such illness in a year. Hgb 10.2, plt 90K, 20% atypical lymphocytes, DAT positive, retic 4.6%, LDH 388, haptoglobin <10, total bilirubin 1.9. Since then the sore throat is easing and fevers are less frequent; still tired. No bleeding, no dark urine. No medications. NKDA. Family history of nasopharyngeal carcinoma in a maternal uncle and gastric cancer in a paternal grandfather.

Exam: Tired but well-appearing. Vitals as recorded. No scleral icterus. Cervical nodes still tender. Spleen palpable, mildly enlarged. No petechiae, purpura or mucosal bleeding. Heart and lungs normal.

Labs today: Hgb 10.6, plt 104K, retic 4.1%.

Impression: Mild autoimmune hemolytic anemia and thrombocytopenia accompanying infectious mononucleosis. Counts already turning upward. Positive heterophile results can persist for months, which may explain the repeated positives this year. Expect both to settle as the infection does.

Recommendations:
1. Observation. No corticosteroid at this hemoglobin with counts improving.
2. CBC weekly for now; first one next week, can be drawn at his PCP's office.
3. No contact sports or heavy exertion while the spleen is enlarged.
4. Seek care for jaundice, dark urine, bleeding or rapidly worsening fatigue.
5. Return visit in about 4 weeks.

Thank you for this referral.

documents.title: Blood Count Today
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hemoglobin up to 11.5 and platelets 131, both moving the right way since last week. Copy sent to hematology. Keep the activity restrictions for now.

documents.title: RE: Blood Count Today
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Nice. I go back to campus Sunday. Can I do next week's blood test there?

documents.title: RE: Blood Count Today
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Yes. Ask campus health to draw a CBC and fax the result to us and to hematology. Fax numbers are on your after-visit summary.

documents.title: Note for school
documents.author: patient
documents.body: My dean's office wants a doctor's note so I can drop to part-time load for the first few weeks without penalty. Is that something you can write?

documents.title: Medical Letter for School
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
To whom it may concern,

Min-jun Tanaka is under my care for a recent medical illness. His recovery is expected to take several more weeks, during which he may have reduced stamina. I support a reduced course load and flexibility with attendance through the end of February 2026. Please contact my office with any questions.

Sincerely,
Primary care physician

documents.title: Hematology Follow-up
documents.author: hematology
documents.body:
Outside hematology group. Follow-up visit 02/06/2026. Received 02/10/2026.

Interval: energy steadily better, attending classes on a reduced load, no fevers for about three weeks. No bleeding or dark urine. Weekly counts trending up.

Exam: Well. No icterus. No cervical adenopathy of note. Spleen not palpable. No petechiae.

Labs today: Hgb 12.6, plt 178K, retic 2.2%.

Impression: Autoimmune hemolysis and thrombocytopenia with mononucleosis, resolving without treatment.

Plan: Stop weekly CBCs. Repeat CBC in about 2 months through his PCP; if normal, he can be discharged from our clinic and we will send a closing letter. Spleen no longer enlarged on exam; return to sports can be decided with his PCP.

documents.title: Hematology letter
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Read hematology's note from last week. Your counts are close to normal, hemoglobin 12.6 and platelets 178. No more weekly blood tests. Let's see you in April with a blood count; the front desk will reach out. Hold off on basketball until that visit.

documents.title: RE: Hematology letter
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Ok thanks. Spring break is the week of March 16, but April is fine, I can come on a Wednesday afternoon.

documents.title: Scheduling
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Called pt to schedule April recheck with CBC per PCP. Booked Wed 4/8 at 4:00.

documents.title: Appointment Cancelled
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt called, has a midterm moved to Wednesday afternoon. Cancelled 4/8, rebooked Wed 4/15 at 4:20.

documents.title: Follow-up - Hemolysis and Thrombocytopenia
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Recheck, about 3.5 months after the January illness with Coombs-positive hemolysis and low platelets. Hematology observed without treatment; Feb counts Hgb 12.6, plt 178K. Feels completely back to normal, full course load again since March. No fevers, sore throats, bruising, bleeding or dark urine. Wants to play intramural basketball this spring.

No medications. NKDA.

Exam: Well. Vitals as charted. Sclerae anicteric. Oropharynx clear. No cervical or supraclavicular nodes. Abdomen soft, spleen not palpable. Skin without petechiae or bruising.

CBC in office: Hgb 14.1, plt 228K, WBC normal.

A/P:
1. Mononucleosis with autoimmune hemolysis and thrombocytopenia, resolved. Counts normal. Removed from active problem list. Will forward today's CBC to hematology for their closing letter.
2. Cleared for all sports.
3. Physical due in the summer; flu and COVID in the fall.

documents.title: CBC
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Yesterday's blood count was entirely normal. Sent a copy to hematology. Enjoy the basketball.

documents.title: RE: CBC

documents.body: Thank you for everything this winter!

documents.title: Hematology Discharge Letter
documents.author: hematology
documents.body:
Outside hematology group, letter dated 04/20/2026, received 04/22/2026.

We reviewed the CBC from 04/15/2026 (Hgb 14.1, plt 228K). His autoimmune hemolysis and thrombocytopenia associated with infectious mononucleosis have resolved without treatment. He is discharged from hematology follow-up. Should anemia, jaundice or low platelets recur, we would be glad to see him again.

Scanned and filed.
